pending_scientific_source_proposal.subject: thm-qftx-scalar-eg-induction
pending_scientific_source_proposal.exact_old: The fixed-annulus Baire argument used in the graph supplier gives, for every real $\omega<d$, a uniform annular estimate $C\rho^{-\omega}p_m$.
pending_scientific_source_proposal.exact_new: Fix a compact annulus $K\subset\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\}$ and a real $\omega<d$. On the complete fixed-support test space $\mathcal D_K$, put $L_\rho(\psi)=\rho^\omega(t_\Gamma)_\rho(\psi)$. Since $\operatorname{sd}_0(t_\Gamma)=-\infty$, for every $\omega$ there is a decay exponent $\eta<\omega$, so $L_\rho(\psi)\to0$ for each fixed $\psi$. On every compact scale interval $[\epsilon,1]$ the scaled tests vary continuously in one fixed-support test space, so $\sup_{0<\rho\le1}|L_\rho(\psi)|<\infty$. The closed sets $E_N=\{\psi:\sup_\rho|L_\rho(\psi)|\le N\}$ cover $\mathcal D_K$. Completeness and Baire under DC, supplied by the already assumed AC, give $\psi_0,m,a>0$ with $\psi_0+\{\zeta:p_m(\zeta)<a\}\subset E_N$ for some positive integer $N$. Subtraction gives $|L_\rho(\zeta)|\le2N$ there; scaling $\zeta=a\psi/(2p_m(\psi))$ yields $|L_\rho(\psi)|\le(4N/a)p_m(\psi)$ when $p_m(\psi)>0$, while $p_m(\psi)=0$ implies $\psi=0$. Hence $|(t_\Gamma)_\rho(\psi)|\le C\rho^{-\omega}p_m(\psi)$ uniformly. This is the fixed-annulus Baire proof, with the arbitrarily negative decay exponent replacing the finite-real-degree hypothesis. [A1, F12]
